new_statements.rule_in_words: The source states that Sabah Malay has no (contrastive) syllable stress: the merger of historical schwa with /a/ yields full homonyms because neither stress placement nor gemination distinguishes them. No position of stress is given; the remark is made in passing in a historical-phonology discussion, not in a dedicated suprasegmental section.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Elsewhere (pp. 58-59) the paper notes expressive vowel lengthening 'pronounced in a high pitch' on deictics (e.g. 'way over there') and describes particles such as bah as attaching to intonational segments; the particle bah is said to add 'mild stress' (emphasis) to the phrase it follows.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (lexical homonymy argument); no phrase-level stress description. Sabah Malay as the Kota Kinabalu / west-coast lingua franca, data from fieldwork in various parts of Sabah. A second-hand anthropological source (Carruthers 2026, snippet only) instead asserts penultimate stress for Sabah Malay; no primary linguistic description supporting that was found.
new_statements.identity_note: Hoogervorst 2011 describes Sabah Malay proper (the Malay lingua franca of Sabah, chiefly the Kota Kinabalu / west-coast variety, with data from various districts) = Glottolog saba1263 / ISO msi. Note that Glottolog's descriptive bibliography for saba1263 also lumps in Singapore Bazaar Malay works (Aye 2005, 2013; Mashudi 1971; Muthiah 2007; McHugh 1948; Peace Corps 1964), which describe a different variety; none of those was used for the statement. Wong 2005 covers the Semporna (east-coast) sub-variety.
